Enjoyed meeting with the Muskingum Valley HR Management Association to talk about what we need to prepare Ohio's next generation of workers. 

Partnerships between local businesses and schools are helping students build real-world skills and prepare for good-paying careers right https://t.co/trZ6mfrnB3

Proud to join my House colleagues on the Capitol steps to honor our nation’s heroes and celebrate Veterans Day. 

Today is a reminder for all of us to be grateful for the sacrifices of those who answered the call to serve. 🇺🇸 https://t.co/2Chrfvwae7
Thank you to the men and women who’ve served and defended our freedom. God bless our veterans! 🇺🇸 https://t.co/lELx1IPJ3C

Today, House Republicans selected Jim Jordan to serve as the next Republican Leader. 

Jim is a dedicated public servant and proud Ohioan who is committed to protecting our freedoms and keeping America on the path to prosperity. 

He knows our nation’s best days are yet to come and is the leader we need to stand firm on common-sense conservative principles that will keep our country strong and secure. 

Jim’s motto is “do what you say you’re going to do.” I look forward to doing exactly that and delivering results for Ohio and the American people.

Ohio continues to be the best place to build, invest, and do business. 💪

Today, Honda announced a new $3 billion investment near Marysville, creating more than 2,000 jobs and demonstrating a continued commitment to Ohio workers and American manufacturing.

Honored to celebrate the brave men and women who have served our country at the Veterans Social in Delaware, OH! Thank you to all our veterans for your courage and dedication to protecting our freedom. https://t.co/vks8eP5Dwz

Thank you to Mrs. Garber and the 4th graders at Nashport Elementary for another great visit! 

It’s an annual tradition to meet with her students, share my journey, and talk about my job serving them in Washington. https://t.co/kzek8RJ0Fc

You can apply for assistance at https://t.co/J6Yk5HqtR2 or by calling 800-621-3362. FEMA and Small Business Administration representatives will also be available at the following locations to help with applications:

https://t.co/kEziQ4Q7Xy

Today in Pleasant City, we honored the five Kachmarik brothers who served our nation during WWII. 

Corporal John Kachmarik was killed in action, and his four brothers passed away in the years since. We will always remember their courage and sacrifice. https://t.co/uKsjnUvy30

Great to spend time with the people who build and make things right here in Guernsey County. 

I appreciated the opportunity to speak at the Guernsey manufacturing appreciation luncheon today to celebrate National Manufacturing Month and recognize the workers and businesses that https://t.co/4HswToj5is

Thanks to the team at Pickerington Surgery Center for taking the time to meet with me and share more about the work they do to care for patients in Pickerington and the surrounding communities. https://t.co/15XTtD8KHM

Great to visit Vermeer Heartland today! I appreciate their investment in our community and am excited to see them expand to Etna. Congratulations on this exciting milestone and best wishes for continued success! https://t.co/J2WviyoyIb

Congratulations to Central Ohio Technical College on the grand opening of Thomas J. Evans Hall!

This new facility will give law enforcement cadets the training and hands-on experience they need to prepare for careers in public safety. 

Thank you to @COTCedu and everyone involved for investing in the next generation of officers and helping keep Ohio communities safe.

Every Ohioan deserves access to quality, affordable health care. Providers like @LowerLightsCHC in Newark are making that happen, connecting patients with critical care regardless of their ability to pay.

I’m grateful for the work they do and will keep fighting to support Federally Qualified Health Centers and the communities that count on them.

Visited Diamond Power in Lancaster today to learn more about their advanced boiler cleaning technology and how they support power generation and industrial operations.

Great to see Ohio-based companies making an impact across the U.S. and beyond. https://t.co/q5GDTFiEqY

Honored to attend the Veterans Appreciation Foundation’s monthly breakfast at the American Legion in Zanesville and present a proclamation to Larry Waltz of Ohio Pottery Zanesville, celebrating 60 years in business! 

Larry’s a proud veteran, dedicated supporter of fellow veterans, and gives back to his community whenever he can. Thank you for your service!

Today, I joined @berniemoreno, leaders from Perry and Muskingum Counties, and representatives from @fema and @SBAgov at the newly opened Disaster Recovery Center in Roseville to discuss the next steps in flood recovery.

Last week, President Trump approved federal disaster relief for communities in OH-12, providing much-needed assistance for Ohio families and businesses as we work to rebuild stronger than before.

Three years after October 7, we remember the 1,200 lives tragically lost and reaffirm our commitment to standing against antisemitism in all its terrible forms.

We stand with the Jewish people around the world and with our ally Israel—which has the right to defend itself, protect its people, and live in peace and security.

posts.text:
JUST ANNOUNCED: I just received confirmation that President Trump has approved Ohio’s major disaster declaration for the devastating flooding in August.

Federal flood relief is now on the way to help Ohio families, businesses, and communities recover and rebuild. But the job isn’t over. 

I will keep working to make sure Ohioans get every resource available to them until our communities are stronger than before.
https://t.co/w3mep3eO4M

Ohio families shouldn’t be subsidizing some of the world’s largest tech companies. 

If data centers are built in Ohio, they should pay for the electricity and infrastructure they need—not force those costs onto families and small businesses. 

No Ohioan should see their electric bill go up just so a data center can be built. 

The Ratepayer Protection Act puts a stop to that and makes sure these companies pay their own way. The House passed this commonsense bill by a bipartisan vote of 417-3, but Senate Democrats blocked it from moving forward. 

Ohioans are already facing rising electric bills, yet Democrats in Washington chose petty politics over protecting Ohio ratepayers.

Bringing costs down for Ohio families means building more homes and cutting the red tape that drives up prices. 🏡

The @HouseGOP led the way on the bipartisan 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, expanding housing supply and making homeownership more attainable for hardworking families.
Wishing all those observing Yom Kippur an easy and meaningful fast. May we all find strength in forgiveness and hope in the year to come. https://t.co/OzNF6daALL

The House unanimously passed my bipartisan Load Forecasting Enhancement Act to help lower energy costs by giving states and utilities better tools to plan and prepare for changing electricity demand.

Planning ahead means savings for Ohioans on their monthly electric bills.

Read more about my bill here👇
https://t.co/22Txx2ilIg
Great meeting today with folks from the Ohio Pork Council to discuss the issues facing our pork industry and how we can continue to strengthen Ohio’s ag industry. https://t.co/0RYhGdSII1

Honored to attend the 9/11 memorial ceremony today at the Ohio Fallen Heroes Memorial in Sunbury. 

On the 25th anniversary of September 11, we remember the lives lost, honor the heroes who stepped up to help others, and pay tribute to the men and women who served in uniform in the years that followed. 

Their courage and sacrifice will never be forgotten.
Shanah Tovah to all celebrating Rosh Hashanah! May the new year be sweet and full of peace, blessings, and good health. https://t.co/2hqTAmP9Gi

Twenty-five years ago today, our nation was forever changed by the tragic events of September 11, 2001.

Today, we remember the nearly 3,000 innocent lives lost and honor the first responders, firefighters, police officers, and everyday Americans who ran toward danger to help others.

In the face of unimaginable tragedy, we saw the courage, compassion, patriotism, and unity that define the American spirit.

We will never forget.

Ohio is helping lead America’s manufacturing resurgence.

In August, I joined @boblatta and @OHIOMFG to discuss what Washington can do to help power our growing manufacturing sector while lowering energy costs for Ohio families. https://t.co/ABmzaNQdbM
Happy Labor Day! Thank you to all the hardworking Ohioans who keep America moving forward. https://t.co/EeycStTZ9a

Today, @SenJonHusted, @berniemoreno, and I urged President Trump to swiftly approve @GovMikeDeWine's request for a major disaster declaration for Ohio following devastating storms and flooding.

Our communities need a helping hand to recover and rebuild, and this declaration would make critical federal assistance available to those who need it.

https://t.co/Bi7qFgrjPZ

roll_calls.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Ratepayer Protection Act (H R 9340)
roll_calls.plain_language: This bill tells state utility regulators to consider making very large power users, such as data centers using 100 megawatts or more, pay the full extra cost of grid upgrades built to serve them. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

If data centers are built in Ohio, they should pay for the electricity and infrastructure they need—not force those costs onto families and small businesses. 

No Ohioan should see their electric bill go up just so a data center can be built. 

The Ratepayer Protection Act puts a stop to that and makes sure these companies pay their own way. The House passed this commonsense bill by a bipartisan vote of 417-3, but Senate Democrats blocked it from moving forward. 

Ohioans are already facing rising electric bills, yet Democrats in Washington chose petty politics over protecting Ohio ratepayers.

roll_calls.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Concur in Senate Adt to House Adt to Senate Adt — Housing for the 21st Century Act (H R 6644)
roll_calls.plain_language: The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act establishes and modifies various federal housing programs. This vote, under suspension of the rules, was on accepting the Senate's latest changes to the bill after the chambers traded versions, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea accepts the Senate's version; a Nay opposes it.
